nodes.name: River phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting algae that start the river's food chain. They feed zooplankton, mussels and filter-feeding fish.

nodes.name: Wild celery & pondweeds
nodes.desc: Underwater plants rooted in the river bed. The FWS and Wikipedia describe submerged vegetation as important for fish and waterfowl. Canvasbacks eat the tubers.

nodes.name: Moist-soil plants
nodes.desc: Plants that sprout on exposed mud flats when floods recede. Their seeds feed ducks.

nodes.name: Cottonwood & silver maple
nodes.desc: Bottomland forest trees that flood each spring. Beavers and deer use them.

nodes.name: Black willow
nodes.desc: Colonizes new sandbars and banks. Beavers, muskrats and deer all browse it.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny animals that graze algae and feed paddlefish, gizzard shad and silver carp.

nodes.name: Freshwater mussels
nodes.desc: The upper river has dozens of mussel species. They filter algae from the water, and freshwater drum eat them. The NPS reports their numbers are recovering.

nodes.name: Aquatic insect larvae
nodes.desc: Larvae living in mud and on wood. They feed on algae and detritus and are a main food for freshwater drum.

nodes.name: Gizzard shad
nodes.desc: A filter-feeding fish and the most important forage fish in the river. Herons, cormorants, pelicans, ospreys, eagles and catfish all eat it.

nodes.name: Silver carp (invasive)
nodes.desc: A filter feeder that eats mostly phytoplankton and also zooplankton. Competes with paddlefish, gizzard shad and young fish. The NPS works to keep invasive carp downstream.

nodes.name: Paddlefish
nodes.desc: A giant filter feeder that eats mainly zooplankton, with a few insect larvae and small fish.

nodes.name: Canvasback
nodes.desc: A diving duck that migrates along the Mississippi Flyway. It eats tubers, buds, seeds, snails and insect larvae, favoring wild celery. The FWS says the upper river supports up to half the world's canvasbacks.

nodes.name: Mallard
nodes.desc: Eats seeds from moist-soil plants and other plant foods in flooded fields and backwaters.

nodes.name: Muskrat
nodes.desc: Lives along banks and marshes, eating aquatic plants.

nodes.name: White-tailed deer
nodes.desc: Browses young trees and shrubs on the floodplain. Coyotes take fawns, and eagles scavenge carcasses.

nodes.name: American beaver
nodes.desc: Cuts cottonwood and willow for food and dams.

nodes.name: Freshwater drum
nodes.desc: Crushes mussels and eats insect larvae and, later in the year, young gizzard shad.

nodes.name: River otter
nodes.desc: Hunts fish along the banks. The NPS notes its return since the 1980s as a sign of better water quality.

nodes.name: Great blue heron
nodes.desc: Wades the shallows spearing fish. The NPS notes herons depend on fish.

nodes.name: Double-crested cormorant
nodes.desc: Dives for fish. The NPS notes cormorants depend on fish.

nodes.name: American white pelican
nodes.desc: Scoops up fish from shallows. Breeds on lakes across interior North America and winters on the Gulf coast, and also follows the Mississippi River in winter.

nodes.name: Osprey
nodes.desc: Dives for fish. The NPS notes ospreys depend on fish.

nodes.name: Flathead catfish
nodes.desc: Mostly eats fish once larger than about 25 cm. Prey includes gizzard shad, drum, carp and crayfish.

nodes.name: Bald eagle
nodes.desc: The FWS counts more than 200 nesting pairs in the refuge and nearby public lands. Eats fish and waterfowl and scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: Lives along the banks, taking fawns, ducks and muskrats. The NPS lists it as a bank dweller.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Powers phytoplankton and the plants of the floodplain.

nodes.name: Flood pulse & river flow
nodes.desc: Spring floods spread water, silt and fish across the floodplain. When the water drops, bare mud flats grow moist-soil plants.

nodes.name: Sediment & nutrients
nodes.desc: Silt carries nitrogen and phosphorus onto the floodplain. Much of it travels downriver to the Gulf of Mexico.

nodes.name: Bacteria & fungi
nodes.desc: Break down leaf litter, dead fish and plants and return nutrients to the water and soil.
